goal: Let the user see a record's state at a glance
how: A .badge whose word says the state and whose tone says what it means: go for done, warn for waiting, danger for failed. It sits in .card-head-right beside a record's title, or in a column of its own in a table.
avoid: A tone with no word, or a semantic tone on a category: a red pill says danger whether or not the data does.

goal: Let the user tell apart categories that have no ranking
how: .badge--cyan, --orange and --teal mean nothing but different, for a type, a queue or a source. Reach for them only after the semantic set does not fit.
avoid: Giving a category a semantic tone, which reads as good or bad.

goal: Let the user see where an item ranks on a scale of severity
how: .badge--sev-1 to --sev-5 is an ordered ramp from critical to planning, and the label carries the rank in words, P2 and High, so the order does not rest on colour.
avoid: A bare coloured pill for a rank: the reader cannot tell P2 from P3 by hue alone.

goal: Let the user see which values an AI filled in, and put one back
how: A .badge-ai button after the value opens a popover saying which agent, from what, how sure, and what was there before, with Revert to the original at its foot. .badge-ai--icon is the sparkle alone, named by a visually hidden span.
avoid: Marking a generated value with no way to see why or to undo it.

goal: Let the user see the filters in force and remove each one
how: A .chip-set under the toolbar with one .chip--active per filter in force, each with a .chip-dismiss button named after the value it removes, then Clear all. The toolbar changes the filters; the chips say what is applied.
avoid: A bare × with no name on the remove button: a screen reader hears only "button".

goal: Let the user see who did something, as a picture, initials or an icon
how: An .avatar holding an image, initials or an icon in that order of preference, with the name in text beside it or in an alt. .avatar--viz-1 to -6 give people in a set their own hue, and .avatar--muted marks an actor with no person behind it.
avoid: An avatar as the only carrier of a name: initials are not a name to a screen reader or to a stranger.

goal: Let the user see at a glance who is involved
how: .avatar-group overlaps the avatars and ends with an .avatar-more count. In a list whose names must line up, two people are an .avatar-pair inside one avatar's square, named once on the wrapper.
avoid: Ringing an avatar inside a group, whose cut-out clips the ring.

goal: Let the user see whether a person is available
how: .avatar-presence puts the state on the avatar's corner as a shape as well as a colour, and the wrapper's aria-label or the text beside it names it. Where there is room the state is written out, with a time: in a meeting until 11:30, or last seen.
avoid: Restyling a presence mark into a plain dot, which loses the shape that carries it for colour-blind readers and forced colours.

goal: Let the user see that they are acting as another person, and stop
how: The user widget shows the person being acted as, .avatar--ring-warn on the avatar and an Acting as badge in place of the e-mail line; its menu says who is really signed in and offers the way back. In a user list the same ring and badge mark that person.
avoid: A ring with no words: write Acting as beside it, and on the trigger's aria-label where a phone hides the badge.

goal: Let the user scan a list of people with their details
how: Each person is a .list-row: the avatar, .list-main with the name as .list-title and the e-mail or role as .list-sub, and a state in .list-meta. In a table cell the same lockup is .list-row--flush.
avoid: Writing a person class of the app's own for the lockup, which the list row already is.
